ns0:table.aria-label: The equations are y equal to 2 x minus 3 and minus 6x plus 3y equal to minus 9. The slope and y intercept of the first equation are 2 and minus 3 respectively. In the second equation, when x is 0, y is minus 3 and when y is 0, x is 3 by 2. We use these points for graphing the lines to determine the point of intersection. The lines are the same. Since every point on the line makes both equations true, there are infinite many ordered pairs that make both equations true. There are infinite many solutions to this system.

ns0:media.alt: A system of two linear equations is shown, enclosed by a blue brace on the left. The first equation is y = 2x - 3, and the second equation is -6x + 3y = -9.

ns0:solution.ns0:para: If you write the second equation in slope-intercept form, you may recognize that the equations have the same slope and same y-intercept.
